newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BK cites poor judgement in UBS investment.
newsitem.headline: BK cites poor judgement in UBS investment.

text.p: BK Vision's investment in Union Bank of Switzerland, which has led to a bitter battle between the bank and the investment trust, in retrospect was based on a poor assessment of the bank's domestic credit portfolio, BK Vision AG president Martin Ebner said on Wednesday.

"We allowed ourselves to be misled by the fact that the UBS was never involved in major loss-making ventures abroad and based on this we expected a higher quality domestic credit portfolio. That was bad judgement on our part," Ebner told reporters at a news conference.
Ebner also said BK Group had made a false assessment of prior management.
"The fact that former UBS management was unable to take criticism proved fatal for the BK Group," Ebner said.
Ebner has been seeking to pressure management to focus more on shareholder value and on improving return on equity.
Earlier on Wednesday Ebner announced plans to appeal a recent ruling by a Zurich court that upheld the UBS plan to adopt a single share structure.
Zurich's Commercial Court in early September upheld the legality of a decision by UBS shareholders in November 1994 to launch a single share.
